rule: Defer reply sentinel couples emitter to classifier read
description: P3 coupling. The defer reply body EMITTED by `plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/reply-resolve.sh` and the deferred-marker predicate READ by `plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/fix-history-classify.jq` are a producer/consumer pair across two files, coupled by ONE byte-anchored sentinel constant. The classifier recognises a thread as already-deferred only when a self-authored body STARTS WITH that constant, so a one-sided edit to the constant silently re-raises every deferred thread as unhandled and drives duplicate defer replies. Two spans carry that coupling and each fails independently. The SOURCE pin is the emitter's body assignment, which places the sentinel ahead of the human-readable citation. The CONSUMER pin is the classifier's executable `startswith` comparison, pinned inside its enclosing `select(...)` so the pin cannot drift onto the sibling `Fixed in` marker test. What this fixture honestly guarantees is exactly that the same sentinel word sequence exists in both of those named spans in these two named files. It does NOT assert that the classifier MATCHES the emitted body, nor that the sentinel occupies byte 0 at run time: a presence pin executes neither side. Behavioural proof of the match lives in `tools/test_reply_resolve.sh` (`defer:body-starts-with-sentinel`, `defer:body-single-line`) and `tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh` (case12, case13). Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a coordinated rewrite that changes the constant consistently in BOTH spans is invisible, and legitimately so — this pin protects the pair from ONE-SIDED drift, never from a joint redefinition; (2) a rewrite-around is outside its reach — a second emission site writing a different body, or a second classifier arm reading a different marker, is in neither pinned span, and a NEW reader that never carries the sentinel at all is an absence defect no fixture in this directory can detect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract; (3) the pin claims nothing about the sibling `Fixed in <SHA>.` prose marker, which keeps its own unanchored pattern read and whose migration is a separate decision recorded in `docs/adr/0032-defer-marker-sentinel-and-agent-layer-home-truth.md`; (4) the tracked home interpolated into the body is citation DATA outside this coupling — the sentinel is emitted unconditionally, so no tracked-home validation guard is part of the pair, and the sanctioned-route coupling that decides when the defer body is emitted at all is guarded by `tests/policy/safety-defer-with-scope-reply-route.json`.
